why: A bookshop chain whose loyalty members spend $21 to $75 each over six months, with spending down year on year as e-readers spread, is believable.
Construction output growth ranging from -7.6% to 8.7% across five years, with letter and 1-10 grades for payment risk and import duty, is believable country data.
A bike shop servicing 58 bikes a month in 75 mechanic hours and 266 bikes in April in 375 hours works out to about 78 to 85 minutes a bike, which is believable.

A large insurer whose 29k ticket-raising staff log 148,000 tickets a year at $2.7m fixed plus $45 a ticket gives about 5 tickets a head and $45 a ticket, and the group sizes add to 29k with per-head cost falling from A to E as stated.
A driving school chain giving about 38,000 to 40,000 lessons a month at roughly $49 a lesson over 25 to 26 teaching days is believable, and profit equals revenue minus costs in both columns.
Burger restaurants serving 650 to 2,100 customers a day with 3 to 8 minute waits, costing $1.2m to open and earning $1 profit a customer, are believable.
Subscription accounting software with small market shares of 0.5% to 8.6% and margins of 15% to 59% abroad falls within what software firms report.
Beef rising from $6.35/kg at the farm gate to $14.30/kg on the plate is believable, the waterfall steps add up, and losing 10% of the weight in trimming is believable.
A repair workshop with about $25k monthly revenue from around 450 to 490 repairs is believable, and the stated margins match revenue minus costs.
Yogurt pots of 0.1 to 0.5 kg priced $0.4 to $1.9, giving about 19 to 21 kg per person a year, match high-consumption countries.
